extracted.intended_audience: Heads of Executive Departments and Establishments; Federal facility and parking managers
extracted.subtask_description: Draft OMB circular setting policy and procedures for charging and managing employee parking at Federal installations to encourage carpooling and transit use, recover costs, and support energy/environmental goals. Includes fee rules, exemptions, managerial obligations, and a comment/phase-in process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parking fee based on fair monthly rental value
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular would establish a parking fee at all Federal installations based on the fair monthly rental value of the parking space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee is to be charged generally at the fair monthly rental value; intent is to set a fee high enough to recover costs and act as an incentive to carpooling. There is an explicit implementation detail/exemption (see the 'minimum fee threshold' metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum fee threshold / exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases no fee will be charged where the rental value is less than $10.00 per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This $10/month threshold is an explicit exemption from charging; it limits administrative burden for very low-value parking spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set fee to balance cost-recovery and administrative efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent is to set a fee high enough to recover its costs and act as an incentive to carpooling, yet not so low that administration of a fee system and parking management would totally consume the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy designers must consider both behavioral incentive effects and the administrative cost of billing/management when selecting fee levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge commercial-equivalent rates to encourage modal shift
rubrics_metrics.description: Charging commercial-equivalent fees for parking is expected to reduce the number of cars in the region and increase carpooling and transit use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo cites studies (Washington Metropolitan Area Council of Governments; comparative study of Federal vs county employees in Los Angeles) supporting that where users pay for parking, carpooling and transit use increase. Policy should target 'commercial-equivalent' pricing where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managers must implement affirmative steps to maximize carpooling
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers at locations which would continue to provide parking without charge will be required to develop and implement affirmative steps for maximizing carpooling among employees and other building tenants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where parking remains free, local parking/facility managers must adopt programs or rules (carpool matching, preferential spaces, rules of utilization) to increase carpool utilization rather than simply continuing subsidies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in period for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular provides for a phase-in period to help employees and agencies adjust carpooling and financial arrangements as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use staged implementation to allow formation of carpools, financial planning by employees, and agency administrative setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary scope: downtown and densely populated suburban facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The pricing policy will primarily affect Federal facilities in downtown locations and densely populated suburban locations, though stricter application may affect all locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy rollout/priority should focus on high-demand urban/suburban sites where commercial-equivalent pricing will have greatest impact on driving behavior and where parking rental value is substantial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy alignment with national energy, transit, and environmental objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal government's historical subsidizing of parking is inconsistent with more recent national policies toward energy conservation, reliance on public transportation, and a cleaner environment; the circular is intended to align Federal parking practice with those policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification and design of fees should explicitly reference energy conservation and environmental goals; expected outcomes include reduced energy consumption, less traffic congestion, increased transit use, greater carpooling, and improved air quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of limited employee hardship and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Charging a commercial rate for parking is not expected to impose a hardship in the vast majority of cases; employees can share costs through carpooling or use public transit which may be more cost effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess impacts on employees; emphasize availability of alternatives (carpools, transit) and use phase-in to mitigate hardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement: invitation for written comments on draft
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are invited to send written comments on the draft circular to Ms. Joyce Walker, Deputy Associate Director, Room 9202, OMB, Washington, D.C. 20503, no later than April 30, 1979.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural requirement for the draft rulemaking/consultation process; comments should be submitted by the stated deadline and to the stated contact to be considered.
